name: Achenseebahn
kurzbeschreibung: Europe's oldest steam-operated cog railway: a nostalgic journey from Jenbach up to Lake Achensee, since 1889.
beschreibung: The Achenseebahn has connected Jenbach railway station in the Inntal valley with Seespitz station on Lake Achensee since 1889 and is regarded as Europe's oldest cog railway operated exclusively with steam locomotives. Over the 6.76-kilometre, metre-gauge route it climbs 440 metres in altitude with a maximum gradient of 160 ‰. Four steam locomotives built in Vienna in 1889 are in service, pulling open and enclosed carriages over the scenic mountain route. In Seespitz there is a direct connection to Achensee shipping; a panoramic train also runs between Seespitz and Eben. The trains run in the season from 1 May to 24 October 2026; in winter the service is suspended. Reservations are only possible for groups of ten or more; tickets are available online and on site.
oeffnungszeiten: Mai–Okt: 3–4 Fahrten täglich (Dampfbetrieb); Nov–Apr: eingeschränkter Betrieb
